content.title: Treatment of adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) and heart failure (HF) in specialized centres
key_recommendations: ACHD patients with chronic HF should be referred to specialized centres.
Specific guidelines for medical treatment of chronic HF in ACHD are lacking; practitioners should follow current HF medical treatment guidelines.
Sacubitril/valsartan may decrease morbidity, but no definitive recommendation can be made due to retrospective/anecdotal nature of observations.

Co-morbidities in HF such as diabetes mellitus, atrial fibrillation (AF), central sleep apnoea (CSA), iron deficiency, and cachexia should be treated according to specific recommendations in the document.

In biventricular circulation, patients with an impaired systemic left ventricle (LV) should be treated with conventional HF therapy; this may be considered for symptomatic patients with a failing systemic right ventricle.
Diuretics are recommended to control symptoms of fluid retention.

Treatment of symptomatic patients with a failing single ventricle (e.g., Fontan circulation), or with a persistent right-to-left shunt, should be carefully initiated with attention to ventricular preload and systemic afterload.

Cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) may be a therapeutic option in ACHD patients with HF, but evidence is lacking in this specific setting; CRT efficacy depends on underlying structural/functional substrate, systemic ventricle anatomy, degree of systemic AV valve regurgitation, primary myocardial disease/scarring, and type of electrical conduction delay.
Treatment of acute HF in ACHD patients should occur in an expert centre with knowledge of inotropes, availability of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and advanced bridging techniques.
Timely evaluation for transplantation by ACHD HF specialists in a transplant centre with ACHD expertise is recommended.
Ventricular assist devices can bridge patients to transplantation or, in a subgroup of patients, may be an option as destination therapy.
clinical_notes: Evidence for many specific therapies in ACHD-related HF is limited; recommendations often rely on extrapolation from general HF guidelines.
Sacubitril/valsartan data in ACHD are retrospective/anecdotal; current statement: may decrease morbidity but insufficient evidence for formal recommendation.
